# Finite-sample dependency uncertainty

# Finite-sample dependency uncertainty — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Finite-sample dependency uncertainty. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-08 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] A surrogate null must match the dependence structure required by the hypothesis. Shorten and colleagues show excessive false positives from naive source time shifts in a common-driver spike-process example; Diks and Fang separately warn that destroying unconditional dependence need not reproduce a conditional-independence null. Their findings concern the tested schemes and processes. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8084348/ · keywords: Finite-sample dependency uncertainty · also: https://www.mdpi.com/1099-4300/19/7/372
- [statement] For time-series significance tests, resampled series must capture the dependence structure compatible with the null hypothesis. The resampling assessment distinguishes constructing an empirical null distribution from merely obtaining a spread of statistic values. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5510825/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For KSG, ordinary resampling with replacement can create duplicate points that appear to be fine-scale information-bearing structure. Holmes and Nemenman show severe upward bias in such bootstrap estimates; Piras and colleagues reproduce this failure. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1903.09280 · keywords: Finite-sample dependency uncertainty · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2211.00024v2
- [statement] Holmes and Nemenman estimate KSG variance using non-overlapping subsamples and a large-sample inverse-sample-size variance model. They warn that overlapping partitions do not supply independent variance samples and that the scaling can fail for small subsamples. Their derivation invokes independent identically distributed contributions; it does not establish validity for autocorrelated lead-lag samples. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1903.09280
- [statement] McAllester and Stratos prove that a distribution-free, high-confidence lower bound on mutual information from N samples cannot exceed O(ln N). The statement limits such lower confidence bounds; it is not a universal ceiling on every point estimate under additional distributional assumptions. (low confidence) — https://proceedings.mlr.press/v108/mcallester20a.html
- [statement] Bootstrap failure is estimator-specific: Piras and colleagues refit a Gaussian mixture model to each bootstrap realization and return the mean and standard deviation of the resulting MI distribution. In their bivariate-Gaussian comparison, GMM-MI agrees with the ground truth while bootstrapped KSG is biased; this experiment does not establish universal calibration. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2211.00024v2 · keywords: Finite-sample dependency uncertainty · also: https://arxiv.org/html/1903.09280
- [statement] Finite-sample uncertainty in mutual-information estimates includes systematic bias as well as sampling variability; error bars alone do not establish that an estimate is unbiased. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1903.09280 · keywords: Finite-sample dependency uncertainty · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2211.00024v2
- [statement] Holmes and Nemenman recommend checking sample-size drift relative to error bars, checking inverse-sample-size variance scaling, and requiring stability across a range of neighbor counts. They caution against declaring an estimator unbiased from stability over only a small sample-size range. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1903.09280

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Finite-sample information estimates can exaggerate weak dependence. Kirkley identifies positive plug-in transfer-entropy bias with sparse bin counts; Chrisman illustrates positive empirical mutual-information bias at weak or absent dependence. These are estimator-specific findings, rather than a universal sign rule for every estimator. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16215 · keywords: Finite-sample dependency uncertainty · also: https://analytica.com/blog/estimation-of-mutual-information/
- [statement] Papana and colleagues find a specificity-sensitivity tradeoff across their resampling settings: more random resampling makes the partial-transfer-entropy test more conservative, and none of their first six methods is optimal across the tested systems. They also report residual spurious couplings in some nonlinear settings. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5510825/
- [statement] GMM-MI provides a concrete implementation of model-based mutual-information uncertainty using Gaussian mixtures and bootstrap. Its authors benchmark finite-sample estimates against known distributions. This supplies an implementation candidate, rather than demonstrated confidence-interval coverage for autocorrelated trading data. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dpiras/GMM-MI/main/README.md · keywords: Finite-sample dependency uncertainty · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2211.00024v2

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For KSG, Holmes and Nemenman propose checking whether the estimate drifts with sample size relative to its sampling standard deviation. Drift substantially exceeding that deviation indicates bias; this diagnostic does not by itself justify extrapolating and subtracting an unknown bias curve. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1903.09280
- [statement] For finite-cardinality streams, Kirkley proposes a finite-data transfer-entropy measure asymptotically equivalent to the standard plug-in estimator and describes a nonparametric significance assessment without simulation. The cited abstract scopes this to small samples or high cardinality; it does not validate continuous financial time series. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16215
